subject: Nate Merritt City Council Candidacy
overview: Host John Petrella interviewed Medford City Council candidate Nate Merritt about his background, reasons for running, and positions on municipal issues. Merritt discussed fiscal responsibility, zoning concerns, commercial tax base sustainability, and public engagement.

items.title: Show Introduction and Guest Welcome
items.summary: Host John Petrella introduced guest Nate Merritt, a candidate for Medford City Council.

items.title: Candidate Background
items.summary: Nate Merritt shared his background as a systems engineer, EMT, private pilot, and Riverside Avenue resident.

items.title: Reasons for Candidacy
items.summary: Merritt explained that he is running for City Council to restore resident voices and address concerns about zoning, rent control, and charter changes.

items.title: Proposed Meeting Management Solutions
items.summary: Merritt proposed that City Council meetings should automatically table remaining agenda items and adjourn at 11:00 PM.

items.title: City Finances and Volunteerism
items.summary: Merritt advocated for an audit of city finances and discussed the bureaucratic challenges he faced when trying to volunteer to repair local park infrastructure.

items.title: Zoning and Housing Positions
items.summary: Merritt expressed concern that rapid rezoning would lead to gentrification, decrease affordable single-family starter homes, and shift tax burdens away from commercial properties.

items.title: Economic Development and Tax Base
items.summary: Merritt emphasized commercial property sustainment and warned that an MBTA purchase of the Riverside Avenue property would eliminate a large source of commercial tax revenue.

items.title: Municipal Spending and Overrides
items.summary: Merritt critiqued the administration's celebration of tax overrides, called for an end to municipal lawsuits, and questioned spending on a poet laureate over road infrastructure.

items.title: Local History and Park Maintenance
items.summary: Merritt spoke on Medford's historical significance and lamented the graffiti and disrepair of historical signs at Mystic River Bend Park despite available CPA funding.

items.title: Personal Interests and Local Concerns
items.summary: Merritt shared his favorite local spots like Donuts with a Difference and playground parks, contrasting them with complaints about potholes and late city council meetings.

items.title: Candidate Contact Information
items.summary: Merritt shared his email address for his grassroots campaign and encouraged residents to meet him at City Council meetings.

items.title: Closing Remarks
items.summary: Petrella concluded the program, thanked Merritt, and invited viewer feedback via email.
